summary: This week brought a mix of congressional pressure and internal debate as the UAP disclosure conversation intensified around several fronts. The Pentagon's All-domain Anomaly Resolution (AARO) office released new documents including authorization protocols and a privacy impact assessment, while lawmakers pushed for release of the so-called "Invasion of Washington" UAP footage and moved toward an FY2026 NDAA briefing deadline on June 30th. A major UAP Disclosure Forum in Washington drew panelists discussing everything from whistleblower protections to the implications of foreign adversaries obtaining UAP technology, though some researchers questioned whether the latest push for disclosure might be a deliberate dead end. Meanwhile, Luis Elizondo denied allegations tying him to secrecy efforts, and questions resurfaced about which high-profile figures like Elon Musk might have knowledge of classified programs. The week underscored a recurring tension: genuine momentum on legislative action coexisting with skepticism about whether real information will actually surface.
